newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Jan non-oil exports up 16 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Jan non-oil exports up 16 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, were up $40 million, or 15.6 percent, at $297 million in January, from $257 million in January 1996, the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) said Wednesday.
January's exports were down $162 million, or 35.3 percent, from $459 million in December, the OCEI figures showed.
Non-traditional exports fell $274 million, or 6.1 percent, to $4.213 billion in 1996.
"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in January with 38.3 percent of total exports. "Chemical products" came next with an 18.5 percent share, then "transport materials" with 6.5 percent.

The United States was the chief market for Venezuela's non-traditional exports in January with 27.3 percent. Venezuela's next largest export market was Colombia with a 15.2 percent share, followed by the Mexico with 4.0 percent, Japan with 2.7 percent and the United Kingdom with 1.3 percent.
